EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
  MINUTES
  November 28, 2016

CALL TO ORDER
CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ called the meeting to order, the time being 7:00 p.m. in the Rolling
Hills Estates City Council Chambers.

COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT
Chairman Velveth Schmitz
Vicki Shinn
Carrie Silvano
Susan Brtis
Patricia Harik
Carol Dean-Porter
Victor Yoo
Pam Schachter*
*Member Schachter arrived at 7:18 p.m.

COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT
Lisa Hawkins
Bill Kemp

STAFF MEMBER PRESENT
Andy Clark, Community Services Director

DRAFT MINUTES OF OCTOBER 24, 2016
MEMBER DEAN-PORTER moved, seconded by MEMBER SHINN

  TO APPROVE THE DRAFT MINUTES OF THE OCTOBER 24, 2016 EQUESTRIAN
  COMMITTEE MEETING AS PRESENTED.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ SO ORDERED.

AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA
None.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
NOVEMBER 28, 2016  1
 NEW EQUESTRIAN/PEDESTRIAN STREET CROSSING PROJECTS
The Community Services Director reported the Assistant City Manager had stated that the
project bid documents were being prepared by Wildan Engineering. He expected to receive
them in December to begin the bid process through January. Following City Council’s award
to the most qualified bidder, he expected both street crossing safety projects to be completed
by Spring 2017. Member Kemp, who had requested this update, will be contacted by staff.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ RECEIVED AND FILED THE REPORT.

PROPOSED HORSE SHOW TRAILER AND CONTENTS DONATION
The Community Services Director discussed the history of the Equestrian Trails Incorporated
(ETI) organization and how it had recently become the non-profit organization, Peninsula
Equestrian Circuit (PEC), with most of the same ETI Board Members. During ETI’s
dissolution process, ETI was required by law to donate the organization’s assets to another
non-profit organization and the Rolling Hills Estates Pepper Tree Foundation had been
selected. He noted that the City’s Foundation does not have a need for the donated horse
trailer or its contents and that there were concerns about future maintenance of the equipment
and the possibility of injuries when used in the arenas resulting in potential lawsuits against
the City. Thus, staff believed that it made more sense to donate it back to essentially the
same organization, Peninsula Equestrian Circuit, made up mostly of ETI Corral #8
organization’s Board Members.

MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER DEAN-PORTER

  TO RECOMMEND THAT THE PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION ADVISORY BOARD
  MAKE A RECOMMENDATION TO THE PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION BOARD OF
  DIRECTORS TO DONATE THE FORMER EQUESTRIAN TRAILS INCORPORATED
  CORRAL #8 HORSE TRAILER AND ITS CONTENTS TO THE PENINSULA
  EQUESTRIAN CIRCUIT ORGANIZATION.

  AYES:  Brtis, Dean-Porter, Harik, Schachter, Chairman Schmitz, Shinn, Silvano,
  and Yoo

  NOES:  None

  ABSTAIN:  None

  ABSENT:  Hawkins and Kemp

CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ SO ORDERED.

PROPOSED HORSE TRAINER FEE CHANGES
CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ provided the Equestrian Committee and audience members an
overview of the equitable Horse Trainer Permit fee change development process, which had

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
NOVEMBER 28, 2016, 2016  2
 commenced over two years ago by the Committee. The Community Services Director
summarized the November 14, 2016 meeting between City staff and horse trainers, noting
that two categories of trainers were being recommended by trainers and staff, instead of three
categories. He noted that by having three categories, hostilities between trainers could occur
and increased City monitoring would likely be needed.

MEMBER SILVANO indicated that City staff needs to increase monitoring the Chandler Park
arena to enforce the rules regarding the number of trainers in this arena. Audience member,
Lisa Baldwin, reported that the issue of too many horse trainers in the Chandler Park arena
was no longer occurring, as they were texting each other the days and times each had
scheduled lessons each week.

MEMBER SCHACHTER clarified that the intent of Category 2 was to issue business licenses
and horse trainer permits to trainers whose primary business takes place outside the Palos
Verdes area and periodically come to the City’s public arenas to give lessons no more than
once per week. She noted that there are no dressage trainers at the level that she and others
have achieved and that higher level instructors are needed from outside our area. Thus,
these horse trainers would be easily identified by other trainers and City staff.

Audience member, Kim Kohles, stated that her horse trainer’s insurance cost her $1,200 per
year. CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ and MEMBER SILVANO responded that all licensed trainers
have to purchase insurance and therefore this will not be considered as part of the horse
trainer permit fee change process. Audience member, Lisa Baldwin, indicated that she was
adding revenue to the City’s general fund by boarding six horses at the Peter Weber
Equestrian Center. CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ reiterated that horse boarding and other
associated trainer costs would not be considered as part of the horse trainer fee change
discussion.

MEMBER YOO inquired whether an on-line calendar for each arena be established. If so, he
believes that the City and Committee can track each horse trainer’s usage to develop an
equitable horse trainer permit fee system. MEMBER SILVANO disagreed, as she believes
that an on-line registration process may make it difficult for some trainers to sign up due to
other trainers monopolizing the on-line calendar registration process.

MEMBER SCHACHTER stated that the diversity in the training disciplines available in the City
is good for the local equestrian community. However, she believes that we have lost the
ability of residents to easily use the arenas for recreational riding with such a focus on
training.

CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ asked whether the Committee had any interest in reconsidering the
three horse trainer permit tiers, perhaps with a lower fee increase for 2017 and 2018.
MEMBER DEAN-PORTER responded that she felt that the two tier process would be best.
MEMBER HARIK indicated that there was a need for a horse trainers who come from outside
the area and many find it more feasible to purchase an annual business license and horse
trainers permit versus a daily horse trainer’s license. In response to CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ’s
inquiry, MEMBER BRTIS stated she preferred the two tier horse trainer permit system.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
NOVEMBER 28, 2016  3
 In response to audience member, Kelly Yates’, inquiry regarding who was complaining about
the current fees being inequitable, MEMBER SHINN responded that the horse trainers only
teaching at private facilities and the Peter Weber Equestrian Center. It was noted that there
has been an increase in the number of horse trainers due to demand from the local
equestrian community and that increasing the permit fees may be a way to limit the number of
trainers from expanding to an overwhelming level.

MEMBER SHINN noted that the City’s costs to maintain the arenas has increased, as the all
the public arenas are now harrowed twice per week. CHAIRWOMAN SCHMITZ provided an
overview of the City’s General Fund, stating that approximately $2 million of the current
budget has been dedicated to equestrian services and capital improvements. She then
requested that an Equestrian Committee member make a motion on this issue.

MEMBER DEAN-PORTER moved, seconded by MEMBER BRTIS

  TO RECOMMEND THAT THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MAKE A
  RECOMMENDATION THAT CITY COUNCIL ADOPT THE TWO CATEGORIES OF
  HORSE TRAINERS PERMIT FEES AS FOLLOWS:
  CATEGORY 1 - HORSE TRAINERS IN RESIDENCE AT A PRIVATE FACILITY AND
  DO NOT USE THE CITY’S PUBLIC ARENAS ($300 BUSINESS LICENSE ONLY)
  CATEGORY 2 - HORSE TRAINERS WHO USE THE CITY’S PUBLIC ARENAS ($300
  BUSINESS LICENSE AND $150 HORSE TRAINERS PERMIT FEE)

  AYES:  Brtis, Dean-Porter, Chairman Schmitz, and Yoo

  NOES:  Harik, Schachter, Shinn, and Silvano

  ABSTAIN:  None

  ABSENT:  Hawkins and Kemp

CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ REPORTED THAT THE MOTION DID NOT CARRY.

CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ asked whether there would be an alternate motion for the Committee
to consider.

MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by MEMBER SILVANO

  TO RECOMMEND THAT THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MAKE A
  RECOMMENDATION THAT CITY COUNCIL ADOPT THE THREE CATEGORIES
  HORSE TRAINERS PERMIT FEES AS FOLLOWS:

  CATEGORY 1 - HORSE TRAINERS IN RESIDENCE AT A PRIVATE FACILITY AND
  DO NOT USE THE CITY’S PUBLIC ARENAS ($300 BUSINESS LICENSE ONLY).

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
NOVEMBER 28, 2016  4
   CATEGORY 2 - HORSE TRAINERS WHO’S PRIMARY BUSINESS IS CONDUCTED
  OUTSIDE OF THE PALOS VERDES PENINSULA AREA AND USE THE CITY’S
  PUBLIC ARENAS NO MORE THAN ONCE PER WEEK ($300 BUSINESS LICENSE
  AND $150 HORSE TRAINERS PERMIT FEE).

  CATEGORY 3 – HORSE TRAINERS WHO’S BUSINESS SIGNIFICANTLY RELIES
  ON THE CITY’S PUBLIC ARENAS AND USES THEM ON A WEEKLY TO DAILY
  BASIS ($300 BUSINESS LICENSE AND $350 HORSE TRAINERS PERMIT FEE FOR
  CALENDAR YEAR 2017 AND $300 BUSINESS LICENSE AND $700 HORSE
  TRAINERS PERMIT FEE FOR CALENDAR YEAR 2018).

  AYES:  Brtis, Dean-Porter, Chairman Schmitz, and Yoo

  NOES:  Harik, Schachter, Shinn, and Silvano

  ABSTAIN:  None

  ABSENT:  Hawkins and Kemp

CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ REPORTED THAT THE MOTION DID NOT CARRY.

CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ asked again whether there would be an alternate motion for the
Committee to consider.

MEMBER HARIK moved, seconded by MEMBER DEAN-PORTER

  TO RECOMMEND THAT THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MAKE A
  RECOMMENDATION THAT CITY COUNCIL ADOPT THE PROPOSED TWO
  CATEGORY HORSE TRAINERS PERMIT FEES AND INCREASE THE CATEGORY 2
  HORSE TRAINER PERMIT FEES BY $50.

  AYES:  Brtis, Dean-Porter, Chairman Schmitz, and Yoo

  NOES:  Harik, Schachter, Shinn, and Silvano

  ABSTAIN:  None

  ABSENT:  Hawkins and Kemp

CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ REPORTED THAT THE MOTION DID NOT CARRY.

CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ asked again whether there would be an alternate motion for the
Committee to consider.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
NOVEMBER 28, 2016  5
 MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by MEMBER SHINN

  TO RECOMMEND THAT THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MAKE A
  RECOMMENDATION THAT CITY COUNCIL ADOPT THE PROPOSED THREE
  CATEGORY HORSE TRAINERS PERMIT FEES WITH THE EXCEPTION THAT: 1)
  CATEGORY 3 HORSE TRAINER PERMIT FEES WOULD INCREASE BY $100 FOR
  CALENDAR YEAR 2017 AND AN UNDETERMINED FEE FOR 2018; 2) ROLLING
  HILLS ESTATES RESIDENTS HORSE TRAINER PERMIT FEES WOULD REMAIN
  AT $150 FOR CALENDAR YEAR 2017; AND 3) CATEGORY 2 HORSE TRAINERS
  SHALL BE DEFINED AS OPERATING THEIR PRIMARY BUSINESS OUTSIDE OF
  LOS ANGELES COUNTY, AS FOLLOWS:

  CATEGORY 1 - HORSE TRAINERS IN RESIDENCE AT A PRIVATE FACILITY AND
  DO NOT USE THE CITY’S PUBLIC ARENAS ($300 BUSINESS LICENSE ONLY).
  CATEGORY 2 - HORSE TRAINERS WHO’S PRIMARY BUSINESS IS CONDUCTED
  OUTSIDE OF THE PALOS VERDES PENINSULA AREA AND USE THE CITY’S
  PUBLIC ARENAS NO MORE THAN ONCE PER WEEK AND HORSE TRAINERS
  WHO RESIDE IN THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES ($300 BUSINESS
  LICENSE AND $150 HORSE TRAINERS PERMIT FEE).

  CATEGORY 3 - HORSE TRAINERS WHO’S BUSINESS SIGNIFICANTLY RELIES ON
  THE CITY’S PUBLIC ARENAS AND USES THEM ON A WEEKLY TO DAILY BASIS
  ($300 BUSINESS LICENSE AND $250 HORSE TRAINERS PERMIT FEE FOR
  CALENDAR YEAR 2017).

  AYES:  Brtis, Dean-Porter, Harik, Schachter, Chairman Schmitz, Shinn, Silvano,
  and Yoo

  NOES:  None

  ABSTAIN:  None

  ABSENT:  Hawkins and Kemp

CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ SO ORDERED.

POTENTIAL USE OF PETER WEBER EQUESTRIAN CENTER
Peter Weber Equestrian Center Concessionaire, Gil Houle, addressed the Equestrian
Committee indicating that there were not consistent time periods each week that could be
made available to the public or to horse trainers. He did note that on a case-by-case basis
that he may allow the Chandler Park arena trainers and students, who are all also Boarders,
to use the arenas when the Chandler Park arena footing is too wet to open. The Community
Services Director indicated that the Concessionaire Agreement does not allow the City to
require the Concessionaire to open the facility’s arenas to the public.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ RECEIVED AND FILED THE REPORT.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
NOVEMBER 28, 2016  6
 EQUESTRIAN ISSUES LOG
Audience member, Susie Lytal, reported that there were on-going issues with the same dog
walker on the Palos Verdes Landfill Loop Trail. The Community Services Director assured
her that the PV Landfill staff and LA County Animal Care and Control had been notified.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ RECEIVED AND FILED THE
EQUESTRIAN ISSUES LOG.

COMMITTEE REPORTS
A.  ADOPT-A-TRAIL REPORTS
It was reported that fencing on the Blossom Trail had fallen over. The magnet was requested
to be run from the Hawthorne Tunnel to Ernie Howlett Park and on the trail behind Dapplegray
Park to the portable toilet. It was also reported that dogs belonging to the new owners of 4
Goldring Place rush to their rear fence when riders pass by. The Community Services Director
assured the Equestrian Committee that the fence would be removed, the magnet would be
run at all the requested trail sites, and that the City’s Zoning and Code Enforcement
Administrator would contact the owners at 4 Goldring Place.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ RECEIVED AND FILED THE ADOPT-A-
TRAIL REPORTS.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS
A.  WATER TRUCK PURCHASE
MEMBER DEAN-PORTER provided the Community Services Director an alternative portable
water storage unit which could be purchased, in lieu of buying a new or used water truck.
This information will be included in the options to potentially acquire a water truck for use in
the Howlett Park horse arenas for the January 23, 2017 Equestrian Committee Meeting.

B.  UNLICENSED EQUESTRIAN SERVICE PROVIDERS
Staff will attempt to identify all the potential equestrian services providers in the City and the
types of business licenses which may apply, and whether permit fees should be developed for
those providing services in public facilities, trails, and parks in a report to the Equestrian
Committee on January 23, 2017.

ADJOURNMENT
CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ thanked MEMBER SCHACHTER for her dedicated service to the City,
as she will be retiring at the end of 2016 from the Park and Activities Commission and
Equestrian Committee.  Committee Members also expressed their gratitude for her
participation on the Committee.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
NOVEMBER 28, 2016  7
 MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER SILVANO

  TO ADJOURN THE EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ ADJOURNED THE MEETING.

The meeting adjourned at 8:37 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,

Andy Clark
Community Services Director
